title: FEMA flood zone and Base Flood Elevation (BFE)
rule: Your flood zone and BFE come from FEMA's flood map (FIRM) for your exact parcel. Manatee County's maps were updated in 2021 and generally dropped BFEs about 2 ft on Longboat Key.
implication: The BFE (plus freeboard) sets how high the lowest floor's bottom must sit. Get the parcel's real zone and BFE before designing anything.

sources.label: LBK Flood Risk & Elevation Certificate Search (Forerunner)
Your Observer: new maps lowered BFE about 2 ft

notes: Could NOT confirm the cited 11-14 ft NAVD88 for 6441 Gulfside Rd. Look the parcel up on Forerunner or the FEMA MSC; a Gulf-front Sleepy Lagoon lot is likely VE (coastal high hazard), but that is unconfirmed.

title: Freeboard (height above BFE)
rule: Florida Building Code requires 1 ft above BFE. Longboat Key requires 3 ft above BFE in V-zones and seaward of the CCCL, or FDEP's elevation if that is higher. Ordinance 2024-03 lets owners add 2 ft more anywhere in town, and Ordinance 2024 (June) allows up to 5 ft total on low-lying lots (at or below 3.5 ft NAVD88).
implication: On a Gulf-front V-zone lot, plan for the lowest structural member at BFE + 3 ft at least, or FDEP's number. Optional extra freeboard can lower insurance costs, but it counts against the height limit.
notes: The V-zone 3 ft rule is from the Town's own FAQ. Confirm the exact current wording in LBK Code Chapter 154.

title: 50% substantial improvement / substantial damage rule
rule: If repairs or improvements cost 50% or more of the building's market value (structure only, not land), the whole building must be brought up to current flood rules, including elevation.
implication: Renovating an older, low house is limited by the 50% cap. A full rebuild on piles is often the realistic route to a hardened compound. Some towns add up the cost of work across several years, so check whether LBK does.

sources.label: FEMA Substantial Improvement/Substantial Damage Desk Reference (P-758)

notes: The 50% threshold is the federal NFIP rule and is verified. Did not confirm whether LBK Chapter 154 counts costs cumulatively (a lookback period).

title: V-zone foundations: open piles/columns and breakaway walls
rule: In V zones, buildings must sit on piles or columns with the lowest horizontal structural member at or above the design flood elevation. Fill can't be used for structural support. Any enclosed space below must use breakaway walls, and it is limited to parking, building access, and storage.
implication: The ground floor can't be a fortified concrete level. Hardening goes into the elevated structure, and the area under the house stays open or breakaway.

sources.label: FBC Residential 2023, R322.3 Coastal high-hazard areas

notes: Standard NFIP/FBC R322.3 requirement. Coastal A zones may have similar local rules.

title: Pile foundation depth
rule: Pile embedment must be designed by an engineer for scour, erosion, and the loads at the site, using a geotechnical report.
implication: Expect deep piles and a soil boring early in design. Pile depth drives cost.

sources.label: FEMA Coastal Construction Manual P-55 (foundation chapter)
FEMA P-550 Recommended Residential Construction for Coastal Areas

notes: Could NOT confirm the cited 10-40 ft to bearing from an official source. Depth depends on the site and needs a geotechnical report. FDEP CCCL permits also review pile tip elevation.

title: CCCL permit from FDEP (seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line)
rule: Construction or excavation seaward of the CCCL needs an FDEP permit under s.161.053, F.S., and Chapter 62B-33, F.A.C. Under s.161.053, most new major habitable structures also can't go seaward of the 30-year erosion projection.
implication: A Gulf-front lot almost certainly needs a CCCL permit. FDEP sets its own structural, elevation, and siting standards and can limit how far seaward you build.

sources.label: FDEP Coastal Construction Control Line Program

notes: Check where the CCCL runs on this parcel using the FDEP CCCL GIS viewer.

title: Gulf waterfront yard: 150 ft from mean high water / ECL
rule: Under LBK Code 158.094, lots that touch the Gulf must keep a 150-ft Gulf waterfront yard. It is measured from the mean high-water line, or from the Erosion Control Line where one has been set. Structures generally can't be built in it.
implication: The buildable area of the 0.71-acre lot can be much smaller than it looks. Map the MHWL/ECL and the 150-ft line before you assume a layout.
notes: Text read from a mirror of the code. Confirm on Municode and check for any listed exceptions (e.g., dune walkovers).

title: Seawall / coastal armoring permitting and height
rule: LBK Ordinance 2024-04 (April 1, 2024) raised the maximum seawall height from 4.5 ft to 6 ft NAVD88, including the cap (Code 151.03). Raising a wall 6 inches or more needs a drainage assessment. On the Gulf, state (FDEP) permits come first, and armoring is generally allowed only when an inhabited structure is threatened.
implication: A 6-ft NAVD88 max is far below storm surge, so a seawall can't serve as flood defense. On the Gulf beach, new armoring is hard to get approved.

sources.label: Your Observer: seawalls up to 6 ft

notes: The cited 6 ft NAVD88 max matches the 2024 ordinance (it replaced 4.5 ft). Read 151.03 directly to confirm the details for Gulf-front walls vs. canal walls.

title: FBC 2023 (8th ed.) design wind speed and Risk Category
rule: Residential homes are Risk Category II. Design wind speed comes from FBC 2023 Figure 1609.3(1), based on ASCE 7-22. Manatee County adopted the state's preliminary 2023 wind map as is.
implication: Design the shell, roof, and connections for at least the mapped speed. A hardened compound should go beyond code (e.g., Risk Cat III/IV loads or FORTIFIED Home).

sources.label: UF GeoPlan / FBC wind speed map report

notes: Could not directly read the mapped Vult at the site. The roughly 150 mph Risk Cat II figure is plausible for coastal Manatee but was not confirmed. Run the ASCE Hazard Tool for the address. Exposure D (open water) likely applies to a Gulf-front lot.

title: HVHZ applicability
rule: The High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) provisions of the FBC apply only in Miami-Dade and Broward counties.
implication: HVHZ is not required in Manatee. You can choose to specify HVHZ/Miami-Dade NOA-approved products as a hardening upgrade.
notes: The HVHZ definition (Miami-Dade and Broward only) is long-standing FBC text.

title: Wind-borne debris region and impact-rated openings
rule: FBC defines the wind-borne debris region as areas within 1 mile of the coast where Vult is 130 mph or more, or anywhere Vult is 140 mph or more. In that region, glazed openings need impact-rated products or approved shutters (tested to ASTM E1996/E1886 or similar).
implication: All windows and doors should be impact-rated, with Florida Product Approval. Larger missile levels (e.g., Level D/E) are a sensible upgrade.
notes: A Gulf-front site is within 1 mile of the mean high water line, so it falls in the WBDR whatever the exact Vult.

title: ICF / reinforced CMU walls
rule: Concrete walls must meet FBC Chapters 19 and 21 (ACI 318 and TMS 402/602). Residential ICF can use FBC-R R608 or an engineered design. In V zones, walls below the DFE must be breakaway, not structural.
implication: ICF or grouted, reinforced CMU is a solid choice for elevated living floors. It can't be used as a solid ground-floor flood wall in a V zone.
notes: Section references are from FBC structure. Specific rebar or thickness numbers were not pulled and need an engineer.

title: Sea turtle-safe lighting
rule: LBK Code Title 9, Chapter 100 (Marine Turtle Protection, amended by Ord. 2021-01) requires shielded, downward, long-wavelength 'turtle-friendly' lighting not visible from the beach, and tinted glass on new beachfront development. FWC and FDEP set the statewide model rules, and CCCL permits impose lighting conditions. Nesting season is May 1 to Oct 31.
implication: Exterior and security lighting for the compound must be FWC-certified, low, and shielded. Window tint (45% transmittance or less is typical) may be required. Floodlit perimeter security on the beach side isn't allowed.

sources.label: LBK Code Ch.100 Marine Turtle Protection

notes: Chapter and ordinance confirmed. The window transmittance number and season dates come from the typical FWC model ordinance and should be confirmed in LBK 100.03.

title: Lot coverage
rule: LBK 158.093 caps coverage by principal and accessory buildings, excluding roof overhangs up to 2 ft, at the limit set for the zoning district. The coverage figure must be certified by a licensed design professional. R-4SF and R-6SF allow 30%, and R-2SF allows 25%.
implication: Confirm this parcel's zoning district (R-?SF). Coverage may be 25% or 30%, and it counts raised decks and stairs.
notes: The roughly 30% cited applies to R-4SF/R-6SF. Did not confirm the district for 6441 Gulfside Rd; use the LBK zoning map.

title: 'Structure/building' definition and the 6-inch rule
rule: LBK 158.144: a 'Building' is any roofed structure, including a screened pool cage. 'Any other structural appendage to a building, including a deck which protrudes more than six inches above finished grade, shall be considered a building, except that permeable planters shall not be considered a building.' The Town's coverage worksheet counts anything more than 6 inches above finished or adjacent grade.
implication: Raised terraces, walls, stairs, and equipment pads more than 6 in. above grade count toward coverage and yard limits. Keep site hardscape at grade where you can. The definition was amended in 2024 and 2025 (Ord. 2024-07, 2025-03), so recheck it.
notes: The quoted wording is from a mirror of 158.144. Recent amendments may have changed it, so check the current Municode text.

title: Setbacks and maximum height
rule: Setbacks (street, side, rear/waterfront) and the maximum height are set per district in LBK Article IV. Height is generally measured from a reference elevation tied to the flood elevation.
implication: Extra freeboard plus piles plus a roof form uses up the height allowance, so check the stories and height before massing.

sources.label: LBK Code Ch.158 Article IV district regs (Municode)

notes: Did not confirm the exact setback and height numbers for this parcel's district.

title: HOA / deed restrictions / Sleepy Lagoon covenants
rule: Private covenants can be stricter than the Town's rules: architecture, height, fences and walls, gates, lighting, rentals, and shared beach access.
implication: Before you offer, pull the recorded plat, restrictions, and easements from the Manatee Clerk. Ask whether any HOA or architectural review exists, and get title commitment exceptions.

sources.label: Manatee County Clerk Official Records search

notes: Did not find any recorded Sleepy Lagoon covenants. Whether an HOA exists is unknown.

title: NFIP, private flood, Citizens, wind, elevation certificate
rule: NFIP caps residential building coverage at $250k, so higher-value homes need private excess flood. Under Florida law (s.627.351(6), F.S.), Citizens policies need flood coverage. Wind is a separate peril in Florida. An Elevation Certificate is required for permits and is key to pricing. LBK is in the NFIP Community Rating System.
implication: Build high (freeboard) and hardened (FORTIFIED, wind mitigation credits) to control premiums. Get quotes before closing.
notes: The NFIP $250k cap is verified federal policy. Citizens eligibility and the timing of its flood mandate, plus LBK's CRS class, were not confirmed this session.

title: Two counties, one town code
rule: Longboat Key straddles Manatee and Sarasota counties. This parcel is in Manatee (property appraiser, tax, recording, county FIRM panels). Town of Longboat Key handles zoning, building permits, and the flood ordinance.
implication: Use Manatee FIRMs and the Manatee clerk, but go to the Town for permits. Don't use Sarasota-side BFEs or rules. Sarasota's 2024 maps differ from Manatee's 2021 maps.

sources.label: Town of Longboat Key Planning, Zoning & Building

notes: FEMA map dates (Manatee 2021, Sarasota 2024) per Your Observer reporting.

title: State moratorium on stricter local rules (SB 250 / SB 180)
rule: Senate Bill 250 (2023) barred local governments near the Ian and Nicole landfalls from adopting more restrictive land development rules. LBK noted it blocked a minimum seawall height. Later legislation reportedly extended or changed this.
implication: Local rules may be frozen or temporarily loosened, which could help or hurt a project. Check status before relying on local changes.

sources.label: Your Observer on SB 250 and LBK

notes: Status in Oct 2026 is not confirmed.
